request: Rewrite this reply for the review thread. The reviewer already knows that the migration fails.
input: Thanks for flagging this! So I dug into the failing migration and here's what I found. The migration adds a NOT NULL column to the orders table, and it turns out that 6 rows in production have no customer_id, which is why the constraint fails. I looked at whether we could backfill them but the customers were deleted in 2023 so there's nothing to backfill from. I also considered making the column nullable but that defeats the purpose of the change. Given all this, I think we should delete the 6 orphan rows first and then re-run the migration, unless finance still needs them for the 2023 audit, in which case we may have to archive them instead.
